clusters.title: How to sell mineral rights without pressure
clusters.answer: Selling mineral rights starts with organizing ownership, lease, division-order, royalty, and offer documents, then comparing the assumptions behind any written offer before deciding whether to proceed.

clusters.title: Mineral rights value and underwriter methodology
clusters.answer: Mineral rights value is directional until ownership, production history, lease terms, operator context, commodity assumptions, and title questions are reviewed together.

clusters.title: Competing offers and buyer comparison
clusters.answer: A mineral-rights offer should be compared by assumptions, deductions, title contingencies, closing timing, buyer disclosures, and written terms rather than the headline number alone.

clusters.title: Inherited mineral rights and probate questions
clusters.answer: Inherited mineral rights usually require gathering probate, deed, division-order, lease, and royalty information before an owner can compare options clearly.

clusters.title: 1031 and tax-sensitive sale questions
clusters.answer: A 1031 exchange or tax-sensitive sale question should be routed to a qualified tax professional; MRX can help organize transaction facts and questions before that conversation.

clusters.title: Royalty checks, production data, and public records
clusters.answer: Royalty checks and public production records help explain current activity, but they do not settle title, lease interpretation, future drilling, or transaction value by themselves.

faq_aeo_answer_blocks.question: What documents should I gather before asking MRX to review a mineral-rights offer?
faq_aeo_answer_blocks.answer: Gather the written offer, recent royalty statements, lease or division order if available, county/legal description, operator letters, and any inheritance or probate documents. If something is missing, note what is missing rather than guessing.

faq_aeo_answer_blocks.question: Can MRX tell me exactly what my mineral rights are worth?
faq_aeo_answer_blocks.answer: No. MRX can prepare a directional underwriter review based on documents and assumptions, but it is not a certified appraisal, legal opinion, tax opinion, or guarantee of a transaction price.

faq_aeo_answer_blocks.question: Which state pages should be published first?
faq_aeo_answer_blocks.answer: Publish Texas first, then New Mexico, Oklahoma, and North Dakota, because the existing site and current content inventory are Texas-heavy and the next clusters should extend from the strongest verified pillar.

faq_aeo_answer_blocks.question: How should state guide pages link to articles?
faq_aeo_answer_blocks.answer: Each state guide should link to one sale-process article, one value/methodology article, one royalty/public-records article, one inheritance/probate article, and one offer-review article, while those articles link back to the state guide only when the state context is materially relevant.

faq_aeo_answer_blocks.question: What has to happen before any Content Genius article is replaced live?
faq_aeo_answer_blocks.answer: One page must pass editorial review, compliance review, local build/lint/typecheck, sitemap inclusion, structured-data validation, GA4 tag/event presence, and read-only GSC inspection before another page is replaced.
